**CCU:** Claude Consumption Unit. A CCU is a unit of measure used solely for Marketplace Platform invoicing. If Customer accesses the Services through certain Marketplace Platforms (e.g., Claude Platform on AWS, Claude in Microsoft Foundry), usage will be invoiced in Claude Consumption Units ("CCU") rather than per MTok. One hundred (100) CCU represents $1.00 USD of fees owed for the Services, calculated at the applicable prices on [claude.com/pricing#api](https://claude.com/pricing#api), after application of any discounts.

### Inference geography

Deployments hosted on Azure can use the US Data Zone Standard deployment type, which keeps inference within the United States. This is equivalent to `inference_geo: "us"` on the Claude API and applies the same 1.1x pricing multiplier. See [Data residency](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency) for details.

## Feature-specific pricing

### Prompt caching

Prompt caching reduces costs and latency by reusing previously processed portions of your prompt across API calls. Instead of reprocessing the same large system prompt, document, or conversation history on every request, the API reads from cache at a fraction of the standard input price.

There are two ways to enable prompt caching:

* **Automatic caching:** Add a single `cache_control` field at the top level of your request. The system automatically manages cache breakpoints as conversations grow. This is the recommended starting point for most use cases.
* **Explicit cache breakpoints:** Place `cache_control` directly on individual content blocks for fine-grained control over exactly what gets cached.

Prompt caching uses the following pricing multipliers relative to base input token rates:

| Cache operation      | Multiplier                                                                                                               | Duration                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| 5-minute cache write | 1.25x base input price                                                                                                   | Cache valid for 5 minutes            |
| 1-hour cache write   | 2x base input price                                                                                                      | Cache valid for 1 hour               |
| Cache read (hit)     | 0.1x base input price (0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1; 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5) | Same duration as the preceding write |

Cache write tokens are charged when content is first stored. Cache read tokens are charged when a subsequent request retrieves the cached content. A cache hit costs 10% of the standard input price, which means caching pays off after one cache read for the 5-minute duration (1.25x write), or after two cache reads for the 1-hour duration (2x write). On Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, a cache hit costs 2.5% of the standard input price ($0.25 USD per million tokens). On Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, a cache hit costs 5% of the standard input price ($0.20 USD per million tokens on Claude Opus 5.5, $0.10 USD on Claude Sonnet 5.5).

These multipliers stack with other pricing modifiers, including the Batch API discount and data residency.

For implementation details, supported models, and code examples, see [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching).

### Data residency pricing

For Claude 4.6 and later models, specifying US-only inference through the `inference_geo` parameter incurs a 1.1x multiplier on all token pricing categories, including input tokens, output tokens, cache writes, and cache reads. On Claude Haiku 5.5, the multiplier also applies to the higher prices for prompts over 100,000 tokens (see [Long context pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#long-context-pricing)). Global routing (the default) uses standard pricing.

This applies to the Claude API (first-party) and Claude Platform on AWS. On Claude in Microsoft Foundry, the same 1.1x multiplier applies to deployments that use the US Data Zone Standard deployment type (see [Inference geography](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#foundry-inference-geography)). Partner-operated platforms (Bedrock and Google Cloud) have independent regional pricing. See [Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) and [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing#claude-models) for details. Earlier models do not support the `inference_geo` parameter and always use standard pricing; requests that include the parameter on these models return a 400 error.

For more information, see [Data residency](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency).

### Fast mode pricing

[Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode), in research preview, provides significantly faster output for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, and Claude Opus 4.8 at premium pricing. Fast mode pricing applies across the full context window, including requests over 200k input tokens. Fast mode is available on the Claude API (first-party) only; it is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms.

| Model                           | Input      | Output     |
| ------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| Claude Opus 5.5                 | $8 / MTok  | $40 / MTok |
| Claude Opus 5 / Claude Opus 4.8 | $10 / MTok | $50 / MTok |

Fast mode is not available on Claude Opus 4.7 (requests with `speed: "fast"` return an error) or Claude Opus 4.6 (requests run at standard speed and are billed at standard rates). See [Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode#supported-models).

Fast mode pricing stacks with other pricing modifiers:

* [Prompt caching multipliers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#prompt-caching) apply on top of fast mode pricing
* [Data residency](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency) multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing

Fast mode is not available with the [Batch API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#batch-processing).

For more information, see [Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode).

### Batch processing

The Batch API allows asynchronous processing of large volumes of requests with a 50% discount on both input and output tokens.

### Long context pricing

Claude 4.6 and later models (except Claude Haiku 5.5) and [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing) include the full [1M token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) at standard pricing. (A 900k-token request is billed at the same per-token rate as a 9k-token request.) Prompt caching and batch processing discounts apply at standard rates across the full context window.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is priced by prompt length: a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens pays higher prices. A request's prompt length counts all of its input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes. Each request is priced on its own: a request over the threshold pays the higher prices even when part of its prompt is a cache hit, and earlier requests keep the prices they were billed at. [Model pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing) and [Batch processing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#batch-processing) list both sets of prices.

These token counts are added to your normal input and output tokens to calculate the total cost of a request.

For current per-model prices, refer to the [model pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing) section.

For more information about tool use implementation and best practices, see [Tool use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview).

### Specific tool pricing

#### Bash tool

The bash tool definition adds the following input tokens to your request. This is in addition to the per-model [tool use system prompt](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#pricing) that applies whenever any tool is present.

| Model                                                 | Additional input tokens |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview | 325 tokens              |
| Claude 4.6 and earlier models                         | 244 tokens              |

Additional tokens are consumed by:

* Command outputs (stdout/stderr)
* Error messages
* Large file contents

See [tool use pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#tool-use-pricing) for complete pricing details.

#### Code execution tool

**Code execution is free when used with web search or web fetch.** When `web_search_20260209` (or later) or `web_fetch_20260209` (or later) is included in your API request, there are no additional charges for code execution tool calls beyond the standard input and output token costs.

When used without these tools, code execution is billed by execution time, tracked separately from token usage:

* Execution time has a minimum of 5 minutes
* Each organization receives **1,550 free hours** of usage per month
* Additional usage beyond 1,550 hours is billed at **$0.05 USD per hour, per container**
* If files are included in the request, execution time is billed even if the tool is not called, because files are preloaded onto the container

Code execution usage is tracked in the response:

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 105,
    "output_tokens": 239,
    "server_tool_use": {
      "code_execution_requests": 1
    }
  }
}
```

#### Text editor tool

The text editor tool uses the same pricing structure as other tools used with Claude. It follows the standard input and output token pricing based on the Claude model you're using.

In addition to the base tokens, the following additional input tokens are needed for the text editor tool:

| Tool                                                                           | Additional input tokens |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `text_editor_20250728` (Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview) | 974 tokens              |
| `text_editor_20250728` (Claude 4.6 and earlier models)                         | 745 tokens              |

See [tool use pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#tool-use-pricing) for complete pricing details.

#### Web search tool

Web search usage is charged in addition to token usage:

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 105,
    "output_tokens": 6039,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": 7123,
    "cache_creation_input_tokens": 7345,
    "server_tool_use": {
      "web_search_requests": 1
    }
  }
}
```

Web search is available on the Claude API for **$10 per 1,000 searches**, plus standard token costs for search-generated content. Web search results retrieved throughout a conversation are counted as input tokens, in search iterations executed during a single turn and in subsequent conversation turns.

Each web search counts as one use, regardless of the number of results returned. If an error occurs during web search, the web search will not be billed.

#### Web fetch tool

Web fetch usage has **no additional charges** beyond standard token costs:

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 25039,
    "output_tokens": 931,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
    "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
    "server_tool_use": {
      "web_fetch_requests": 1
    }
  }
}
```

The web fetch tool is available on the Claude API at **no additional cost**. You only pay standard token costs for the fetched content that becomes part of your conversation context.

To protect against inadvertently fetching large content that would consume excessive tokens, use the `max_content_tokens` parameter to set appropriate limits based on your use case and budget considerations.

Example token usage for typical content:

* Average web page (10 kB): \~2,500 tokens
* Large documentation page (100 kB): \~25,000 tokens
* Research paper PDF (500 kB): \~125,000 tokens

#### Computer use tool

Computer use follows the standard [tool use pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#pricing). When using the computer use tool:

**Toolset definition overhead:** Declaring `computer_toolset_20260801` with its default members adds about 4,500 input tokens to a request (about 4,590 on Claude Sonnet 5 and about 4,520 on the other supported models), which covers the member tool definitions and the tool use system prompt. Disabling `zoom` with `configs` removes about 410 of those tokens. The exact count for a request is reported in the response `usage`, and you can estimate it in advance with the [token counting endpoint](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting).

**Earlier tool versions:** The following figures apply to the `computer_20251124` and `computer_20250124` tool versions, not to `computer_toolset_20260801`:

* System prompt overhead: 466–499 tokens added to the system prompt
* Tool definition: about 735 input tokens per tool definition (measured with `computer_20250124`)

**Additional token consumption:**

* Screenshot and zoom images returned in tool results, billed as image input (see [Vision pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision#evaluate-image-size))
* Tool execution results returned to Claude

<Note>
  If you're also using bash or text editor tools alongside computer use, those tools have their own token costs as documented in their respective pages.
</Note>

#### Browser use tool

Browser use follows the standard [tool use pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#pricing). When using the browser use tool:

**Toolset definition overhead:** Declaring `browser_toolset_20260801` with its default members adds about 6,600 input tokens to a request (about 6,670 on Claude Sonnet 5 and about 6,610 on the other supported models), which covers the member tool definitions and the tool use system prompt. Enabling all four optional members adds about 880 tokens, and disabling members with `configs` reduces the count. The exact count for a request is reported in the response `usage`, and you can estimate it in advance with the [token counting endpoint](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting).

**Additional token consumption:**

* Screenshot and zoom images returned in tool results, billed as image input (see [Vision pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision#evaluate-image-size))
* Text tool results returned to Claude, such as accessibility trees, page text, and console or network entries

<Note>
  If you also use the computer use tool, bash tool, text editor tool, or your own tools alongside browser use, those tools have their own token costs as documented on their respective pages.
</Note>

## Claude Managed Agents pricing

[Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) is billed on two dimensions: tokens and session runtime.

### Tokens

All tokens consumed by a Claude Managed Agents session are billed at the rates shown in [Model pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing). [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#prompt-caching) multipliers apply identically. Web search triggered inside a session incurs the standard $10 per 1,000 searches. On [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#claude-platform-on-aws-pricing), session token and runtime charges convert to Claude Consumption Units at the standard rate. [Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#fast-mode-pricing) premium pricing applies when an agent's `model.speed` is set to `"fast"`.

The [data residency multiplier](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#data-residency-pricing) also applies: when an agent's `model.inference_geo` is pinned to `"us"`, tokens consumed by sessions running that agent are billed at 1.1x the standard rates, the same multiplier that applies to US-only inference on the Messages API.

The following Messages API modifiers do **not** apply to Claude Managed Agents sessions:

| Modifier                                                                                                  | Why it doesn't apply                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Batch API discount](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#batch-processing)           | Sessions are stateful and interactive. There is no batch mode. |
| [Cloud platform pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#cloud-platform-pricing) | Not available on partner-operated cloud platforms.             |

### Session runtime

| SKU             | Rate                   | Metering                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Session runtime | $0.08 per session-hour | `running` status duration |

Runtime is measured to the millisecond and accrues only while the session's status is `running`. Time spent `idle` (waiting for your next message or a tool confirmation), `rescheduling`, or `terminated` does not count toward runtime.

<Note>
  Session runtime replaces the [code execution](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#code-execution-tool) container-hour billing model when using Claude Managed Agents. You are not separately billed for container hours on top of session runtime.
</Note>

### Worked example

A one-hour coding session using Claude Opus 5 that consumes 50,000 input tokens and 15,000 output tokens:

| Line item       | Calculation              | Cost       |
| --------------- | ------------------------ | ---------- |
| Input tokens    | 50,000 × $5 / 1,000,000  | $0.25      |
| Output tokens   | 15,000 × $25 / 1,000,000 | $0.375     |
| Session runtime | 1.0 hour × $0.08         | $0.08      |
| **Total**       |                          | **$0.705** |

If prompt caching is active and 40,000 of the input tokens are cache reads:

| Line item             | Calculation                   | Cost       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- |
| Uncached input tokens | 10,000 × $5 / 1,000,000       | $0.05      |
| Cache read tokens     | 40,000 × $5 × 0.1 / 1,000,000 | $0.02      |
| Output tokens         | 15,000 × $25 / 1,000,000      | $0.375     |
| Session runtime       | 1.0 hour × $0.08              | $0.08      |
| **Total**             |                               | **$0.525** |

## Additional pricing considerations

### Cost optimization strategies

When building agents with Claude:

1. **Use appropriate models:** Choose Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for most production workloads, and Opus for the most complex reasoning
2. **Implement prompt caching:** Reduce costs for repeated context
3. **Batch operations:** Use the Batch API for non-time-sensitive tasks
4. **Monitor usage patterns:** Track token consumption to identify optimization opportunities

<Tip>
  For high-volume agent applications, contact the [enterprise sales team](https://claude.com/contact-sales) for custom pricing arrangements.
</Tip>

### Rate limits

Rate limits vary by usage tier and affect how many requests you can make:

* **Start tier:** Entry-level limits for getting started
* **Build tier:** Increased limits for growing applications
* **Scale tier:** Highest standard limits for production workloads

For detailed rate limit information, see [Rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits).

For limits beyond the Scale tier or custom pricing arrangements, [contact the sales team](https://claude.com/contact-sales).

### Volume discounts

Volume discounts may be available for high-volume users. These are negotiated on a case-by-case basis.

* Standard usage tiers use the pricing shown in [Model pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing)
* Enterprise customers can [contact sales](mailto:sales@anthropic.com) for custom pricing
* Academic and research discounts may be available

### Enterprise pricing

For enterprise customers with specific needs:

* Custom rate limits
* Volume discounts
* Dedicated support
* Custom terms

Contact the sales team at [sales@anthropic.com](mailto:sales@anthropic.com) or through the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/usage/limits) to discuss enterprise pricing options.

## Billing and payment

* Billing is based on actual monthly usage
* All payments are in USD
* Credit card and invoicing options available
* Usage tracking available in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/)

## Frequently asked questions

### How is token usage calculated?

Tokens are pieces of text that models process. How many tokens the same text produces depends on the model's tokenizer, the language, and the type of content. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models. To see how many tokens a request uses on a specific model, count it with [token counting](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting) and that model's ID.

### Are there free tiers or trials?

New users receive a small amount of free credits to test the API. [Contact sales](mailto:sales@anthropic.com) for information about extended trials for enterprise evaluation.

### How do discounts stack?

Batch API and prompt caching discounts can be combined. For example, using both features together provides significant cost savings compared to standard API calls. See [prompt caching pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#prompt-caching) for how the multipliers interact.

### What payment methods are accepted?

Major credit cards are accepted for standard accounts. Enterprise customers can arrange invoicing and other payment methods.

For additional questions about pricing, contact [support@anthropic.com](mailto:support@anthropic.com).

The Python SDK has a client-side `mask` callback and separate server-side PII settings.

**Client-side masking (runs in your process, before export)**

Pass a callback to `neatlogs.init()` through the `mask` parameter. The callback receives each telemetry item and returns it, possibly modified. The docs say that if the callback raises an exception or times out, the affected item is dropped rather than exported unmasked.

```python
import neatlogs

SENSITIVE_KEYWORDS = ("api_key", "secret", "token", "password", "email", "phone")

def redact(item, *, context=None):
    attrs = item.get("attributes", {})
    for key in list(attrs):
        if any(word in key.lower() for word in SENSITIVE_KEYWORDS):
            attrs[key] = "***"
    return item

neatlogs.init(mask=redact)
```

Python also accepts `None` as a return value, which exports the mutated clone. The docs don't say whether this matches API key values inside free-text content, so your callback may need pattern matching for that.

**Per-span masking**

`span()` and `trace()` also accept `mask`. As the docs put it, a per-span callback "applies only to that span and takes precedence over the client's global callback." It does not apply to child or sibling spans.

```python
@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", mask=redact)
def lookup_customer(email: str):
    ...
```

**Server-side PII redaction (project-wide policy)**

You can configure this in the dashboard under **Settings → PII Redaction**, or set it from `init()` with these parameters:

- `pii_enabled`
- `pii_entities`
- `pii_span_types`

```python
neatlogs.init(
    pii_enabled=True,
    pii_entities=["PERSON", "EMAIL_ADDRESS"],
    pii_span_types=["LLM", "TOOL"],
)
```

The docs warn that these are "project settings, not per-process filters," so they change the saved policy for every application and the dashboard in that project. Omit an option to keep its existing value. The docs don't list which entity types are supported beyond the examples above.

**Things to keep in mind**

- Client-side and server-side controls are separate. A local mask doesn't change the server policy, and the server options don't hash content locally.
- Masking covers trace and log export only. Managed prompts sent through the prompt API are not rewritten, so transform those in your application code first.
- If data must never leave your infrastructure, the docs recommend the `mask` callback as the first control.

Anthropic list prices per million tokens (input / output): **Opus 5.5 $4 / $20**, **Sonnet 5.5 $2 / $10**, **Haiku 5.5 $0.10 / $0.50**.

---

❓ **Q18** - **What Gemini is for**: You said to use Gemini "instead of Bedrock". Bedrock was only ever the backup provider, so I read Gemini as the **second provider behind `llm.py`**. Claude remains the main provider (Q14). When an Anthropic call fails with a 5xx, 429 or timeout and retries are used up, `llm.py` switches to Gemini for that call and records a `fallback:gemini` span. That adds a sixth recovery path to the §4.5 list, which we can show to the judges. I'll pick the Gemini model in step 2 by listing what your key can access, not from memory.

➡️ Yes. Gemini is the failover provider, not the main one. (If you meant Gemini as the *main* LLM to save money, say no and I'll redo the model split.)

---

❓ **Q19** - **Opus clashes with the $0.20 cap**: This is a rough estimate, not a measurement. A plan call (~8k tokens in / 1k out) costs about $0.05. Five recovery decisions cost about $0.10. Self-audit on ~10 findings costs about $0.18. With Opus doing all three, a run comes to roughly **$0.33**, well over the cap. Options:
- (a) Opus handles plan + `decide:recovery` only. Sonnet handles self-audit verdicts and report prose. Haiku handles extraction and JSON re-asks. Estimated ~$0.20.
- (b) Raise the per-run cap to $0.40 and keep Opus for audit.

# CLAUDE.md — Spend Radar (neatHack 2026)

You are building **Spend Radar** with Akarsh (team **qwep**, solo) for **neatHack**, a 48-hour online AI-agent hackathon run by neatlogs. This file is the full brief: the rules, the scoring, what to build, the order to build it, and what evidence to produce. Read all of it before writing code. Re-read "Hard rules" whenever you are unsure.

Source of rules: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (fetched 10 Oct 2026). Build-log skill: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill. If anything here conflicts with those pages, the pages win; tell Akarsh.

---

## 0. Hard rules (breaking any of these can disqualify us or cost money)

1. **All code is written during the hackathon**: Sat 10 Oct 2026, 12:30 PM IST → Mon 12 Oct 2026, 11:55 PM IST. Do not copy in code from any earlier project, including Akarsh's other repos (Glance, SecureAgent, etc.). Open-source libraries installed via pip/npm are fine.
2. **Public GitHub repo**, with commits made throughout the event so judges can see the dates. Commit small and often (at least every hour of work). Never squash or rewrite history. The repo's first commit must be after 12:30 PM IST, 10 Oct.
3. **Must use all three: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai**, each with a clear role, and the demo must cover all three.
4. **Demo video ≤ 3 minutes** (not stated on the rules page; we keep it as the safe limit).
5. **Submission** = a public quote-post on X of the official neatlogs submission post, between **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00 PM and 11:55 PM IST**, containing team name (qwep), project name, public repo link, demo link. Late = not judged.
6. **Do not use Glance** or any of Akarsh's existing projects in this repo.
7. **No fabricated numbers anywhere** — not in code, README, report, posts, or the video. Every confidence score is computed. Every metric comes from a saved scorecard or trace link. Unmeasured numbers in drafts are written as `{N}` placeholders and filled only from a real run. Estimates are labelled as estimates.
8. **Never commit secrets.** `.env` (git-ignored) plus `.env.example`. Secrets never appear in commits, logs, neatlogs traces, or screenshots (see §6.1).
9. **Zero spend, everywhere.** No billing on any service. Free tiers only for LLMs (§3). Never add credits or a payment method to OpenRouter, Google AI Studio, or anything else. cfo.ai is cancelled in Settings → Billing immediately after signup. AWS use stays inside the organisers' allowance and instances are stopped whenever idle. Anything that could incur a charge → ask Akarsh first.
10. **Real customer finance data never goes through free LLM providers.** We only send fictional Acme data and public Crustdata facts.

---

## 1. Judging (optimise for this, in this order)

| Category | Weight | What the judges look at |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | How well the agent handles a substantial task start to finish |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | How effectively they were used to build, improve, and plan a business around the agent |
| Demo video | 20% | How clearly it explains the agent and the use of all three tools |
| Building in public | 15% | What was shared publicly during the hackathon, tagged #neatHack |
| Usefulness & originality | 10% | A real problem solved in a new way |

Focus areas for the agent: **planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration**. The design must visibly hit every one.

**Evidence judges require (each claim must be checkable):**
- *Agent improved*: runs before and after a change (neatlogs traces) with numbers compared (§7).
- *Used neatlogs*: trace links or screenshots.
- *Used Entire*: checkpoints or entire-graph output from the repo.
- *Used cfo.ai*: a business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway.
- *Recovers from failure*: a run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next.
- *Built in public*: links to posts tagged #neatHack.
- *Wrote code during hackathon*: public repo with dated commits.

Judges: 2 from Entire (devrel, solutions engineer), 2 from neatlogs (founder, head of product engineering), 1 founder of Orchestrator.inc. They build agent/dev tooling. They will notice fake metrics and will appreciate real traces, real bugs found and fixed, and clean engineering.

Prizes: 1st $2,000 + $5,000 Dodo credits; 2nd $1,000 + $3,000; 3rd $500 + $1,000; each winner gets 3 months neatlogs Pro. Separate $500 community award for genuine community interest. Winners announced 16 Oct.

---

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**
> Input: a folder of the company's finance files (budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, spend policy) and a hard-coded competitor list (`data/acme/competitors.yaml`).
> Output: a report per spend category with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Category scope (decided):**
- **Competitor comparison is on people cost only**: engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing *team*. Each category states "people cost only" in the report. Policy rules in `policy.yaml` are written against people cost.
- **Infra/cloud** is checked only internally (our invoices vs budget vs policy). No competitor estimate for it.

**Competitors:** real dev-tools / AI-infra companies. Step 1 probes 7 candidates — Datadog, Grafana Labs, Chronosphere, Honeycomb, Arize, New Relic, Sentry — and keeps the 4–5 with the best Crustdata coverage. Never include neatlogs or Entire (their people judge). Competitor auto-selection is a stretch goal only.

**Our company:** "Acme Observability Inc." — fictional, labelled as such everywhere.

---

## 3. Tool stack and the role of each tool

| Job | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trace every LLM call, tool call, retry, decision, state change; find bugs; compare runs | **neatlogs** (required) | Docs: https://docs.neatlogs.com, https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk. Integrate before agent logic so the first run is traced. Details in §6. |
| Repo context and checkpoints for the coding agent (you) | **Entire** (required) | Already enabled for Claude Code (`entire enable --agent claude-code`; re-run after any `git init`). Checkpoints add an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer to commits. Evidence: `entire checkpoint list/explain`, `entire graph stats`, entire-graph output → `evidence/entire/`. |
| Business plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway | **cfo.ai** (required) | Akarsh signs up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks and cancels the subscription immediately. He builds the model; you prepare inputs (§9). |
| Competitor data | **Crustdata** | 5,000 credits. Auth: `authorization: Bearer <key>`, `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`. `POST /company/enrich` (`fields`: headcount incl. `by_role_absolute`/`by_role_percent`, growth `mom/qoq/six_months/yoy/two_years`; funding) ≈ 2 credits/company. `POST /job/search` (`job_details.title`, `job_details.category`, `metadata.date_added`; `group_by` aggregations, `limit:0` for aggregation-only) at 0.03 credits/result. No headcount timeseries — trend comes from growth fields. Confirm all fields with the Step 1 probe; check real prices via `GET /account/endpoints`. |
| LLM — primary | **Google Gemini, free tier only** (`google-genai>=1.55.0`) | Role split: Pro → plan, `decide:recovery`, self-audit; Flash → report prose; Flash-Lite → extraction, title classification, JSON re-asks. **Read the real model list and rate limits from AI Studio in Step 2; do not trust model names from memory.** If Pro's daily quota is too small, the eval decides whether Flash is good enough for planning (becomes a case study). |
| LLM — secondary | **OpenRouter, `:free` models only** | Never add credits. A guard in `llm.py` refuses any model ID not ending in `:free`. Free limits without credits: 20 req/min, 50 req/day. Roles: (1) cross-provider failover after Gemini retries + model fallback are exhausted; (2) independent second opinion in the self-audit, max 5 calls/run, only on findings Gemini marked uncertain or overturned. Pick the model in Step 2 by listing free models via the API; it must support JSON output or tool calling and pass our Pydantic schemas. |
| Hosting (optional) | **AWS** | Organisers' allowance ($25, us-east-1 only) covers EC2, Lambda, IAM and load balancers only; Bedrock is not available. One instance, t3.micro or t3.small, in Hackathon_VPC, for a live report / scheduled runs. Stop it whenever not needed (the access page does not track spend). Never on the critical path. AWS keys stay in `.env` and never appear in commits, logs, traces or screenshots. |
| File parsing | `openpyxl` (xlsx), `pdfplumber` (PDF), Gemini PDF input as fallback for scanned PDFs | Test both PDF routes early; keep the one that works. |
| Language | Python 3.11+, plain hand-written loop, Pydantic for state | No heavy agent framework. |

All LLM calls go through one module, `llm.py`: `llm(role=..., ...)` picks the model per role, enforces the `:free` guard, the rate limiter, and the quota ledger, and records provider/model on every span.

---

## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

### 4.6 Budgets and quotas

- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**
> Input: a folder of the company's finance files (budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, spend policy) and a hard-coded competitor list (`data/acme/competitors.yaml`).
> Output: a report per spend category with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Category scope (decided):**
- **Competitor comparison is on people cost only**: engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing *team*. Each category states "people cost only" in the report. Policy rules in `policy.yaml` are written against people cost.
- **Infra/cloud** is checked only internally (our invoices vs budget vs policy). No competitor estimate for it.

**Competitors:** real dev-tools / AI-infra companies. ## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**

> Output: a report per spend category with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Category scope (decided):**

**Competitors:** real dev-tools / AI-infra companies. All LLM calls go through one module, `llm.py`: `llm(role=..., ...)` picks the model per role, enforces the `:free` guard, the rate limiter, and the quota ledger, and records provider/model on every span.

---

## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

### 4.6 Budgets and quotas

- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

content.content:
## Request body

Send `POST https://api.crustdata.com/job/search` with these headers: `authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`, `content-type: application/json`, and `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`.

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "op": "and",
    "conditions": [
      { "field": "company.basic_info.primary_domain", "type": "=", "value": "stripe.com" },
      { "field": "metadata.date_added", "type": "=>", "value": "2025-01-01" },
      { "field": "metadata.date_added", "type": "<", "value": "2026-01-01" }
    ]
  },
  "limit": 0,
  "aggregations": [
    {
      "type": "group_by",
      "field": "job_details.category",
      "agg": "count",
      "size": 10
    }
  ]
}
```

## Filter syntax

- **Company name:** `{ "field": "company.basic_info.name", "type": "=", "value": "Stripe" }`. The doc lists `(.)` for broader multi-word matching.
- **Company domain:** `{ "field": "company.basic_info.primary_domain", "type": "=", "value": "stripe.com" }`
- **Company id:** `{ "field": "company.basic_info.company_id", "type": "=", "value": 631394 }`. This is the filter alias for `crustdata_company_id`.
- **Date added:** `metadata.date_added` with `=>` (inclusive) and `<` (exclusive). Date-only values are read as midnight UTC.

Combining conditions on the same exact-match field with `and` returns nothing: "Exact-match AND on the same field always returns zero results."

## Aggregations, limit, and cursor

- **`group_by`:** `job_details.category` is in the groupable allowlist. `agg` currently supports only `"count"`, and `size` defaults to 100 (max 1000).
- **`limit`:** Max 1000. The doc says to "Set `limit: 0` when you only want aggregation output."
- **`cursor`:** Resend the same `filters`, `sorts`, and `fields`, adding `cursor` set to the previous response's `next_cursor`. A `null` cursor means the end of results.

## Abridged example response

The doc doesn't include a `job_details.category` response. This is built from the documented shape, and the counts are illustrative:

```json
{
  "job_listings": [],
  "next_cursor": null,
  "total_count": 1200,
  "aggregations": [
    {
      "type": "group_by",
      "field": "job_details.category",
      "buckets": [
        { "key": "Engineering", "count": 700 },
        { "key": "Sales", "count": 300 },
        { "key": "Operations", "count": 120 },
        { "key": "Others", "count": 80 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The doc documents `metadata` on buckets only for `company.basic_info.company_id` groupings, so I left it out here.

## Credit costs

The provided content doesn't mention credit costs for aggregations or for `limit: 0`. It only says that `limit: 0` returns aggregation output without job rows.

content.content:
## Request body schema

```json
{
  "domains": ["string"],
  "professional_network_profile_urls": ["string"],
  "names": ["string"],
  "crustdata_company_ids": [0],
  "fields": ["string"],
  "exact_match": true
}
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default |
| - | - | - | - |
| `domains` | string[] | One identifier type required | none |
| `professional_network_profile_urls` | string[] | One identifier type required | none |
| `names` | string[] | One identifier type required | none |
| `crustdata_company_ids` | integer[] | One identifier type required | none |
| `fields` | string[] | No | `["basic_info"]` |
| `exact_match` | boolean | No | `null` |

"Submit exactly one identifier type per request." Mixing identifier types is not supported.

## Required headers

- `authorization: Bearer REDACTED`
- `content-type: application/json`
- `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`

## Valid `fields` values

`basic_info`, `headcount`, `funding`, `locations`, `taxonomy`, `revenue`, `hiring`, `followers`, `seo`, `competitors`, `social_profiles`, `web_traffic`, `employee_reviews`, `people`, `news`, `software_reviews`, `public_launches`, `market_intel`, `technographics`, `social_posts`, `reviews`

The section names for headcount, funding, and hiring are exactly `headcount`, `funding`, and `hiring`. The reference says that `technographics` and `social_posts` are gated add-ons and that `social_posts` is only available on API version `2025-11-01`.

## Example request

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.crustdata.com/company/enrich \
  --header 'authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-version: 2025-11-01' \
  --data '{
    "domains": ["retool.com"],
    "fields": ["basic_info", "headcount", "funding", "people"]
  }'
```

## Abridged example response

The reference does not include a headcount response sample. This is an illustrative sketch built from the documented key paths. The values are invented, and the role and region key names are placeholders because the reference doesn't define them.

```json
[
  {
    "matched_on": "retool.com",
    "match_type": "domain",
    "matches": [
      {
        "confidence_score": 1.0,
        "company_data": {
          "crustdata_company_id": 12345,
          "basic_info": { "name": "Retool", "primary_domain": "retool.com" },
          "headcount": {
            "total": 500,
            "by_role_absolute": { "<role>": 120 },
            "by_role_percent": { "<role>": 24.0 },
            "by_region_absolute": { "<region>": 300 },
            "growth_percent": {
              "mom": 1.2,
              "qoq": 3.5,
              "six_months": 6.0,
              "yoy": 15.0,
              "two_years": 40.0
            },
            "growth_absolute": {
              "mom": 6,
              "qoq": 17,
              "six_months": 28,
              "yoy": 65,
              "two_years": 140
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Key paths

| Path | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `company_data.headcount.total` | Total employee count |
| `company_data.headcount.by_role_absolute.<role>` | Employee count per role |
| `company_data.headcount.by_role_percent.<role>` | Share of employees per role |
| `company_data.headcount.by_region_absolute.<region>` | Employee count per region |
| `company_data.headcount.growth_percent.{mom,qoq,six_months,yoy,two_years}` | Percentage change over each window |
| `company_data.headcount.growth_absolute.{mom,qoq,six_months,yoy,two_years}` | Absolute employee change over each window |

The period keys here differ from `/company/search`. That endpoint "returns the same growth data under **different period keys**" (`1m`, `3m`, `6m`, `12m`). The mapping is `mom` to `1m`, `qoq` to `3m`, `six_months` to `6m`, and `yoy` to `12m`. `two_years` has no equivalent on `/company/search`.

"""Throwaway Step 1 spike: which Crustdata fields exist for our candidate competitors?

Calls company enrich (one batched request) and a jobs-by-category aggregation per
company, saves the raw JSON to cache/crustdata/probe/, and prints a field-coverage
summary. Run: uv run spikes/crustdata_probe.py
"""

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = ["httpx", "python-dotenv"]
# ///

import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
from dotenv import load_dotenv

BASE = "https://api.crustdata.com"
CANDIDATES = {
    "Datadog": "datadoghq.com",
    "Grafana Labs": "grafana.com",
    "Chronosphere": "chronosphere.io",
    "Honeycomb": "honeycomb.io",
    "Arize": "arize.com",
    "New Relic": "newrelic.com",
    "Sentry": "sentry.io",
}
OUT = Path("cache/crustdata/probe")


def save(name: str, payload: object) -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (OUT / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))


def main() -> None:
    load_dotenv()
    key = os.environ.get("CRUSTDATA_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        sys.exit("CRUSTDATA_API_KEY missing from .env")
    headers = {
        "authorization": f"Bearer {key}",
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "x-api-version": "2025-11-01",
    }
    client = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, headers=headers, timeout=60)
    stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

    # Real per-endpoint prices for this account, before spending anything.
    r = client.get("/account/endpoints")
    save("account_endpoints", {"status": r.status_code, "fetched_at": stamp, "body": r.json() if r.is_success else r.text})
    print(f"account/endpoints -> {r.status_code}")
    if "--prices-only" in sys.argv:
        return

    r = client.post(
        "/company/enrich",
        json={"domains": list(CANDIDATES.values()), "fields": ["basic_info", "headcount", "funding", "hiring"]},
    )
    enrich = r.json() if r.is_success else r.text
    save("enrich", {"status": r.status_code, "fetched_at": stamp, "body": enrich})
    print(f"company/enrich -> {r.status_code}")

    jobs = {}
    for name, domain in CANDIDATES.items():
        r = client.post(
            "/job/search",
            json={
                "filters": {"op": "and", "conditions": [
                    {"field": "company.basic_info.primary_domain", "type": "=", "value": domain},
                ]},
                "limit": 0,
                "aggregations": [{"type": "group_by", "field": "job_details.category", "agg": "count", "size": 50}],
            },
        )
        jobs[name] = r.json() if r.is_success else r.text
        save(f"jobs_{domain}", {"status": r.status_code, "fetched_at": stamp, "body": jobs[name]})
        print(f"job/search {domain} -> {r.status_code}")

    # Coverage summary
    print("\n== coverage ==")
    by_domain = {}
    if isinstance(enrich, list):
        for entry in enrich:
            matches = entry.get("matches") or []
            by_domain[entry.get("matched_on")] = matches[0]["company_data"] if matches else None
    for name, domain in CANDIDATES.items():
        cd = by_domain.get(domain) or {}
        hc = cd.get("headcount") or {}
        roles = hc.get("by_role_absolute") or {}
        growth = hc.get("growth_percent") or {}
        fund = cd.get("funding") or {}
        j = jobs.get(name)
        buckets = []
        if isinstance(j, dict):
            for agg in j.get("aggregations") or []:
                buckets = agg.get("buckets") or []
        print(
            f"{name:13} total={hc.get('total')!s:6} roles={len(roles):2} "
            f"growth={sorted(growth)} funding_keys={len(fund)} "
            f"jobs_total={j.get('total_count') if isinstance(j, dict) else 'ERR'} job_cats={len(buckets)}"
        )
        if roles:
            print(f"   role keys: {sorted(roles)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

# Step 1 — Crustdata probe findings (10 Oct 2026, ~13:40 IST)

Raw responses: `cache/crustdata/probe/` (git-ignored). Script: `spikes/crustdata_probe.py`.

## Credits
- Balance 5200 → 5172: **28 credits spent**.
- `/company/enrich` = 2 credits/company (7 companies = 14). It ran twice because the first probe version re-enriched during the jobs test (14 wasted). The probe now reuses cached enrich data.
- `/job/search` with `limit: 0` + `group_by` aggregation: **0 credits** (balance unchanged across 7 calls).
- `/account/credits` and `/account/endpoints`: free.

## Fields that exist (all 7 companies)
| Field | Present | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `headcount.total` | yes | |
| `headcount.by_role_absolute` | yes, 10–16 roles | Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Product Management, Support, … **No ML/AI role.** |
| `headcount.by_role_growth_6m_pct` / `_yoy_pct` | yes | per-role growth |
| `headcount.timeseries` | yes | weekly total headcount back to 2021 |
| `headcount.by_function_timeseries` | yes | monthly per-function counts |
| `headcount.by_skill_absolute` | yes | skills, e.g. Python; too coarse for ML |
| `funding` | yes | total_investment_usd, last_round_*, last_fundraise_date, acquisitions |
| `hiring` | 6 of 7 | openings_count, by_function_qoq_pct/6m_pct, open_jobs_timeseries, recent_titles_csv. **Chronosphere: all null.** |
| `news` | yes | dated articles with URLs (useful for self-audit: layoffs/freezes) |
| `/job/search` category buckets | yes | `job_details.category` is noisy ("Engineering", "Engineering ", "Engineering and Information Technology", "Others"); `total_count` is all-time unless filtered by `metadata.date_added` |

## Decision (Step 1)
- **Engineering, Sales, Marketing**: use `by_role_absolute` directly (signal 1), cross-checked against `by_function_timeseries` trend and open-role mix (signal 2).
- **ML/AI**: no role-level number exists → `classify_titles` (LLM) over job titles filtered by date, with a 30-title hand-labelled eval set. The ML/AI estimate = engineering headcount × the ML share of recent engineering hiring, labelled as an estimate.
- Job-category buckets are normalised in Python (strip, map variants) before use.

## Competitor set
Acme is fictional at ~300 people, so we compare against peers of similar scale, plus one larger reference:
- **Honeycomb** (294), **Sentry** (448), **Arize** (242, AI-infra), **Chronosphere** (139), **Grafana Labs** (1,910).
- Substitute pool: New Relic (3,095), Datadog (10,482). These are too large to be in the median by default.
- Chronosphere has no `hiring` data. That gives us a real case for the "competitor with partial data" recovery path.
EOF
mkdir -p data/acme && cat > data/acme/competitors.yaml <<'EOF'
# Real companies; data from Crustdata. Chosen from the Step 1 probe (spikes/FINDINGS.md).
# Acme Observability Inc. itself is FICTIONAL.
competitors:
  - {name: Honeycomb, domain: honeycomb.io}
  - {name: Sentry, domain: sentry.io}
  - {name: Arize, domain: arize.com}
  - {name: Chronosphere, domain: chronosphere.io}
  - {name: Grafana Labs, domain: grafana.com}
substitutes:  # used, in order, when a competitor has no usable data
  - {name: New Relic, domain: newrelic.com}
  - {name: Datadog, domain: datadoghq.com}
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='hackathon.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("  - Tests run: none yet (no code).\n","""  - Tests run: none yet (no code).
- **13:45 IST — Step 1 done.** Crustdata probe: 28 credits (14 wasted on a duplicate enrich; fixed). All 7 candidates have role-level headcount, timeseries, funding, news; Chronosphere lacks hiring data; no ML/AI role exists, so ML/AI uses title classification. Competitors: Honeycomb, Sentry, Arize, Chronosphere, Grafana Labs (see `spikes/FINDINGS.md`).
  - Tests run: probe script against live API (7 enrich, 7 job aggregations).
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

## Span Kinds

**Decorator-eligible kinds** (`@neatlogs.span()` / `trace()`):
- **WORKFLOW**: Top-level entry point for one complete agent run or request.
- **AGENT**: An autonomous unit that reasons and decides what to do next.
- **CHAIN**: A fixed sequence of steps that runs in a set order without deciding anything.
- **TOOL**: A single callable action an agent invokes, such as an API call or lookup.
- **RETRIEVER**: A step that fetches documents or chunks.
- **EMBEDDING**: A step that generates vector embeddings.
- **GUARDRAIL**: A safety, policy, or content-moderation check.
- **MCP_TOOL**: A tool called through the Model Context Protocol.

**Created with `trace()` or auto-instrumentation:**
- **LLM**: A call to a language model.
- **RERANKER**: A step that re-scores and re-orders retrieved documents.
- **VECTOR_STORE**: A direct vector database operation, such as indexing or querying.

**Produced automatically:**
- **TASK**: A discrete unit of work, such as a CrewAI task or an async batch-job submission.
- **EVALUATOR**: An evaluation or scoring step.
- **HTTP**: An actionable HTTP failure from legacy or external telemetry. NeatLogs SDKs don't create these.
- **LOG**: A structured log line captured inside a span, created with `neatlogs.log()`.

Note: `@neatlogs.span()` accepts only the eight decorator-eligible kinds. `RERANKER`, `VECTOR_STORE`, and `LLM` require `trace()`.

## Examples

**Nesting spans:** Decorate a workflow entry point and its child steps. Nested spans attach to their parent automatically.

```python
@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")
def handle_request(user_input: str):
    return check_order(user_input)

@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="check_order_status", tool_name="check_order_status")
def check_order(order_id: str) -> dict:
    ...
```

**Setting attributes:** Use `set_attribute` inside a `trace()` block. For example, a retriever span can record its query and result count:

```python
with neatlogs.trace("retrieve_docs", kind="RETRIEVER") as span:
    span.set_attribute("neatlogs.retriever.query", query)
    span.set_attribute("neatlogs.retriever.top_k", top_k)
```

Other documented attribute namespaces include `neatlogs.reranker.*`, `neatlogs.guardrail.*`, and `neatlogs.vectordb.*`.

**Recording errors:** The provided content doesn't document an error-recording API, so I can't give a verified example. Check the Python or TypeScript SDK reference for this.

## Python SDK reference (from the page)

The page doesn't include a complete `init()` signature, a session/thread/run ID parameter, or a way to get the current trace ID or URL. Those gaps are noted below.

### `neatlogs.init()`

Call it once, before importing any library you want auto-instrumented. The page says: "Call `neatlogs.init()` once, then wrap your AI client with `neatlogs.wrap(...)`."

```python
neatlogs.init(
    api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"],   # default: NEATLOGS_API_KEY env var
    endpoint="https://ingest.neatlogs.com",   # EU: https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com
    workflow_name="my-app",                   # default: script filename
    instrumentations=["openai"],
    tags=["prod"],
    user_id="svc-billing",                    # operator/service identity, not end-user
    capture_logs=False,
    log_level="INFO",
    sample_rate=1.0,
    flush_interval=5.0,
    batch_size=100,
    mask=None,                                # callable: client-side telemetry transform
    pii_enabled=None,                         # overrides project setting
    pii_entities=None,                        # e.g. ["PERSON", "EMAIL_ADDRESS"]
    pii_span_types=None,
    debug=False,
    tracer_provider=None,                     # private provider you created
    register_shutdown_handlers=True,
    uploads_enabled=False,
)
```

The page doesn't list `isolate` as a usable option. It is deprecated, and Neatlogs is always isolated.

### Flush before exit

```python
neatlogs.flush()     # force immediate export
neatlogs.shutdown()  # stop the background thread
```

For scripts and CLI tools, call both at the end. For long-running servers, call them once at shutdown, not per request. `neatlogs.flush_all()` drains the default pipeline and every live secondary client.

### `@neatlogs.span(...)`

```python
@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name="get_order_status")
def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> dict:
    ...
```

Parameters: `kind` (required), `name`, `role`, `goal`, `tool_name`, `parameters`, `description`, `capture_input`, `capture_output`, `mask`, `capture_stdout`.

`kind` values: `WORKFLOW`, `AGENT`, `CHAIN`, `TOOL`, `RETRIEVER`, `EMBEDDING`, `GUARDRAIL`, `MCP_TOOL`. Other values raise `ValueError`.

`name` is the label in the tree. `tool_name` is the identifier the dashboard groups on.

### `neatlogs.trace(...)`

```python
with neatlogs.trace("retrieve", kind="RETRIEVER") as span:
    span.set_attribute("neatlogs.retriever.query", query)
```

Signature: `trace(name, kind=None, system_prompt_template=None, user_prompt_template=None, version=None, mask=None)`. The page does not show an `attributes` parameter. Set attributes on the returned span with `set_attribute`.

`RERANKER` and `VECTOR_STORE` are only available through `trace()`.

### Trace IDs and URLs

The page doesn't document a way to get the current trace ID or trace URL.

### Session, thread, and run IDs

`init()` has no session, thread, or run ID parameter. The page says session and end-user identity go through `neatlogs.identify(...)`, not `wrap()` kwargs. It refers to `/sdk/sessions` for details, which are not included here.

### Environment variables

The page names only two:
- `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`: project API key, read by `init()` if `api_key` is unset.
- `NEATLOGS_UPLOADS_ENABLED`: enables typed-media and oversized-OTLP uploads.

**`neatlogs.identify` signature:** The page doesn't give a formal signature. It shows usage in Python:

`with neatlogs.identify(session_id="child_123", parent_session_id="parent_456", session_custom_fields={...}):`

The reference table lists the TypeScript form as `identify({sessionId}, fn)` and the Go form as `Identify(ctx, IdentifyOptions{SessionID})`.

**How sessions group traces:** Each conversation turn is its own trace. Traces that share a `session_id` are grouped into one session. The page says, "Traces sharing a `session_id` are grouped under one session." If you omit `session_id`, the backend sets it to the trace ID, so that trace becomes a single-turn session.

**Setting the session:**
- **On the trace root:** Pass `session_id` to `trace()` or `@span` in Python.
- **Wrapper-only code:** Wrap the call in `identify()`. The page notes it "does not carry across separate requests or processes, so re-supply it every turn."
- **HTTP API:** Set the `neatlogs.session.id` attribute on the root object.

**Multi-turn example:** Three turns of one conversation, each run under the same session ID, produce three traces in one session. In Python, each turn uses:

`with neatlogs.trace("chat_turn", session_id="conv_42"):`

**Trace IDs or links:** The page doesn't explain how to retrieve trace IDs or dashboard links. The only related details are the default `session_id = trace_id` behavior and the `neatlogs.session.id` attribute.

"""Secrets must never leave the process in a neatlogs telemetry item."""

from spendradar.tracing import MASK, mask_secrets, scrub_text

FAKE_GOOGLE = "AIza" + "S" * 35
FAKE_OPENROUTER = "sk-or-v1-" + "a" * 40
FAKE_CRUSTDATA = "cd_live_0123456789abcdef"


def test_known_key_formats_are_scrubbed():
    text = f"key={FAKE_GOOGLE} other={FAKE_OPENROUTER} auth=Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv"
    out = scrub_text(text, secrets=[])
    assert FAKE_GOOGLE not in out and FAKE_OPENROUTER not in out
    assert "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv" not in out


def test_env_secret_values_are_scrubbed_anywhere(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("CRUSTDATA_API_KEY", FAKE_CRUSTDATA)
    item = {
        "name": "act:crustdata_company",
        "attributes": {
            "input": f'{{"headers": {{"x": "{FAKE_CRUSTDATA}"}}}}',
            "nested": [{"note": f"used {FAKE_CRUSTDATA} here"}],
        },
    }
    out = mask_secrets(item)
    assert FAKE_CRUSTDATA not in repr(out)


def test_secret_named_attributes_are_blanked_but_token_counts_kept():
    item = {"attributes": {"api_key": "whatever-value", "gen_ai.usage.input_tokens": 120, "authorization": "x"}}
    out = mask_secrets(item)["attributes"]
    assert out["api_key"] == MASK and out["authorization"] == MASK
    assert out["gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"] == 120
EOF

"""Step 2 spike: one traced Gemini call + a custom TOOL span, and find the trace id."""

import os

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv(".env")
from spendradar.tracing import init_tracing, shutdown_tracing  # noqa: E402

init_tracing("probe-step2", ["variant:probe"])
import neatlogs  # noqa: E402
from google import genai  # noqa: E402  (constructed after init)

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])


@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="act:echo", tool_name="echo")
def echo(x: str) -> str:
    return x


with neatlogs.trace("probe_run", kind="WORKFLOW", session_id="probe-step2") as span:
    print("span type:", type(span).__name__, [a for a in dir(span) if "context" in a.lower() or "id" in a.lower()][:10])
    try:
        from opentelemetry import trace as ot

        ctx = ot.get_current_span().get_span_context()
        print("otel trace id:", format(ctx.trace_id, "032x"))
    except Exception as e:
        print("otel lookup failed:", e)
    echo("hello")
    r = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", contents="Reply with one word: traced")
    print("llm:", r.text)
shutdown_tracing()
EOF

"""Deliberate fault injection for recovery traces (`--inject target:fault`).

Each injected fault fires once per process. Injected runs are tagged
`inject:<spec>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

_active: set[str] = set()
fired: list[str] = []


def configure(specs: list[str]) -> None:
    _active.clear()
    _active.update(specs)


def active() -> list[str]:
    return sorted(_active | set(fired))


def fire(spec: str) -> bool:
    if spec in _active:
        _active.discard(spec)
        fired.append(spec)
        return True
    return False
EOF
